claim: Single-occupancy travel uses one vehicle per person; sharing vehicles reduces the vehicle count and vehicle mass allocated to each traveler, while efficient street modes can carry more people in the same width.

entry.title: One person. An entire car.
entry.question: How much vehicle does it take to move one person?
entry.answer: Sharing a vehicle spreads its space and mass across more people. Sixty solo drivers need sixty cars; four per car need fifteen.
entry.explanation: An interactive essay separating vehicle occupancy, street capacity, fuel-energy conversion and illustrative vehicle mass per traveler.
entry.qualification: Vehicle counts are an illustrative model, not measured road area or real-world occupancy. Capacity ranges describe peak conditions; energy estimates describe specified test cycles. Mass per person is not energy efficiency or a lifecycle footprint.
entry.whyCare: A street can be full of vehicles while doing surprisingly little to move people.

evidence.scope: Illustrative group of 60 travelers with 1, 2 or 4 people per car, including drivers; one bus with 60 passengers, excluding its driver. Global Street Design Guide capacity ranges for a 3-m lane or equivalent width under peak conditions with normal operations. U.S. DOE/EPA test-cycle energy estimates. Illustrative 2,000 kg car, excluding occupants.
evidence.dataAsOf: 2016 street design guide, reproduced in 2018 presentation; DOE EV summary September 16, 2024; undated DOE/EPA gasoline page; original illustrative model October 2026
evidence.denominator: People per vehicle; people per hour in a 3-m lane or equivalent width; percent of fuel energy in the gasoline vehicle; kg of illustrative vehicle per occupant. These denominators are not interchangeable.
evidence.methodology: Vehicle counts: 60/n for n=1,2,4; bus illustration assumes 60 passengers. Mass allocation: 2000/n kg for n=1,2,3,4 (rounded only for display). Capacity ranges copied as factual values from Prati 2018 slide 23 (PDF page 23), with 3-m scope supplied by the Global Street Design Guide. Gasoline 18–25% energy to wheels in combined 55% city/45% highway test cycle. EV 87–91% includes net regenerative recovery; excludes lifecycle and electricity generation. No claim that 96% of energy is wasted moving vehicle mass. No causal congestion or citywide emissions estimate.
